newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans 98 primary budget deficit 0.5 pct GDP.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans 98 primary budget deficit 0.5 pct GDP.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has sent an outline of the 1998 budget to his government, putting the deficit, excluding debt servicing, at no more than 0.5 percent of gross domestic product, the presidential press service said.
"In 1999, that indicator should be brought down to zero," Yeltsin was quoted as saying in the press service statement, which was released on Wednesday.

Yelstin ordered the government to change its policy on the securities market substantially. "At the top of the list will not be budget needs but limits on the negative influence on economic growth of the burden of internal debt servicing," the Kremlin said.
Russian Economic Trends Economist Al Breach said Russia would pay about three percent of GDP both this year and next year in interest on domestic GKO Treasury bills and OFZ discount bonds.
He said Russia's primary deficit in 1997 was planned at 3.5 percent of GDP, according to most Russian government calculations.
But that includes 1.5 percent of foreign debt servicing which is generally not considered part of the primary deficit. It was not clear if Yeltsin was including foreign debt servicing in his figures.
